entries.claim: Fix 1 names the new test subdirectory `tests/apply/concurrent/`, which is the name of a stdlib package. It tells the executor to lay it out 'the way tests/api/surface and tests/api/login sit under tests/api', and both of those carry an `__init__.py`. The plan never says to leave the new directories without one.
entries.failure_scenario: The executor copies the cited pattern and adds tests/apply/concurrent/__init__.py. tests/apply has no __init__.py, so the package root is computed as `concurrent`, and pytest's default prepend import mode tries to import `concurrent.test_apply_queue`. asyncio has already loaded the stdlib `concurrent` (asyncio_mode=auto), so that import fails with ModuleNotFoundError and the file is never collected. mypy (files includes "tests", strict) maps the same file to the module `concurrent.test_apply_queue`, which shadows the stdlib `concurrent`, and is expected to error. Either way `make check` goes red. tests/presets/integrity/ has no such clash. Fix: rename the directory to a non-stdlib name, or state that the new directories get no __init__.py. Without __init__.py, collection is fine: the five new basenames are unique across tests/ and scripts/.
